record.field: Everything Operations, Front Desk, HR, Finance and the Director need to get a client set up and a roster running end to end in DeployGuard ERP -- built directly from DogForce's own production system.

This course gets you rostering in DeployGuard ERP, end to end. It's built from our own system, not a generic tutorial -- every screen it shows is the one you'll actually use.

What changed recently, and why it matters:

  • The Clients & Sites menu used to be a cluttered command center. It's now one button -- "Set up a new client" -- plus four simple destinations. If you remember it as complicated, that's fixed.
  • Rosters now carry a sign-off sheet: Front Desk, the General Manager, HR, Finance and the Director each sign off on a roster once it's generated. This does not stop the roster from running -- guards get posted immediately. Sign-offs are accountability, not a gate.
  • Daily attendance posting now needs Front Desk to review it, separately from whoever posted it. If you post attendance yourself, you can no longer also review your own posting.

Work through this course in order. Each "Do it" lesson has a "Try it in DogForce ERP" button that takes you straight to the real screen -- do the real thing, then come back and mark the lesson done.

Six roles touch a roster from draft to paid. Find yours:

  • Operations drafts the roster. Once you generate it, it's live -- guards can be posted against it immediately.
  • Front Desk cross-checks the roster after it's generated, and separately reviews daily attendance postings that Operations makes. You cannot review a posting you made yourself.
  • General Manager validates the roster -- a second set of eyes before it goes further.
  • HR confirms the roster for payroll and checks hours are fairly shared across guards (the Hours Equity Audit).
  • Finance releases payments and audits the roster against billing.
  • Director has final oversight -- and, on this system, full operational and administrative access, since the Director also rosters personally when needed.

Every sign-off is logged with who signed and when -- nothing here is anonymous, and nothing here blocks the guards from working while it happens.
Watch: Setting Up a New Client

Video Walkthrough: Setting Up a New Client in 5 Steps

In DeployGuard ERP, onboarding a client takes you through an integrated 5-step wizard. There's no need to manually visit five separate menus. Everything connects automatically.

Starting Point: Open the Clients & Sites menu and click the prominent "Set up a new client" button.

Step-by-Step Breakdown:

  1. Step 1 — Client Information: Pick an existing partner or enter a new company name, primary contact person, email, and phone number.
  2. Step 2 — Security Sites: Add one row per physical site requiring security guards. Enter Site Name (e.g. Head Office, Kalahari Mine Warehouse), a short unique Site Code (e.g. HQ, WH-1), and street address. You can always add additional sites later.
  3. Step 3 — Shift Requirements: For each site, define the guarding requirements:
    • Post Type: Static Guard, Gate / Access Control, Patrol, Control Room, or Site Supervisor.
    • Shift Template: Day Shift (06:00–18:00), Night Shift (18:00–06:00), 8-Hour Day (08:00–16:00), or Relief.
    • Guard Count: Number of guards required on duty during that shift.
    Billing Rates Flexibility: If client billing rates or guard wage rates are not finalized yet, leave them at zero! You can still generate and run rosters immediately. Billing and payroll will simply flag them as pending review.
  4. Step 4 — Billing Mode: Configure how the client will be invoiced: Fixed Monthly Rate, Per Shift Rate, Per Hour, or Milestone, along with payment terms (e.g. 30 days).
  5. Step 5 — Summary Review & Instant Roster Batch: Check the review table. If any required information is missing, the wizard indicates the exact step to fix. Tick "Create the first roster batch" and select the starting month, then click Create client.
Result: In one single click, the client record, security sites, shift requirements, billing terms, and first draft roster batch are generated and linked.
Do It: Set Up a New Client

One wizard does the whole chain: client, sites, shift requirements, billing, and the first roster batch. Nothing is saved until the last step.

  1. Step 1 -- Client. Pick an existing client, or type a new company name and its contact details.
  2. Step 2 -- Sites. Add one row per site the client needs guarded. Just a name, code and address -- you can add more sites later.
  3. Step 3 -- Shift Requirements. For each site, pick a post type (Static Guard, Gate, Patrol, Control Room, Site Supervisor), a shift (Day, Night, 8h, Relief), and how many guards. Bill/pay rates can be left at zero for now -- you'll still be able to roster, you'll just see a reminder that billing is incomplete.
  4. Step 4 -- Billing. Set how this client is invoiced (fixed monthly, per shift, per hour, or milestone).
  5. Step 5 -- Review. Check the summary. If anything is missing, it's listed here with which step to go back to. Tick "Create the first roster batch" and pick the month, then click Create client.

Now try it for real. Click "Try it in DogForce ERP" below, and either set up a real new client or walk through the wizard with one that already exists (you can cancel at the end without saving). Come back here and mark this lesson done once you've been through all five steps.

Video Walkthrough: Sites, Posts & Shift Requirements

Every security operation is organized around physical sites and their contracted shift requirements. Here is how DeployGuard ERP structures them for effortless management.

1. Grouped Sites List View

The Sites list is grouped by client so you can scan all active sites at a glance. You can expand or collapse client groups or use the search bar to locate any site by name or code.

2. Client 360 View — The Security Sites Tab

Opening any client record reveals the Security Sites tab. This single view displays:

  • All physical sites operated under that client.
  • Active security contracts, tender agreements, and start/end dates.
  • Live shift requirements and required guard headcounts.

3. The 3 Essential Tabs on a Site Form:

  1. Posts & Shifts: Shows all active posts and shift templates for this site.
    • Post Types: Static Guard, Gate, Patrol, Control Room, Site Supervisor.
    • Shift Templates: Day (06:00–18:00), Night (18:00–06:00), 8-Hour Day (08:00–16:00), Relief.
    To adjust guard counts or add new shifts without re-running the onboarding wizard, simply add or edit rows directly in this tab.
  2. Contacts & Location: Holds site contact names, emergency phone numbers, and optional GPS geofencing coordinates. GPS is never required to save a site.
  3. Notes & Exclusions: Special site instructions (e.g., specific gate procedures) and the Guard Exclusion List. If a client requests that a guard not be deployed to their property, add the employee here; the system's rostering auto-allocation will automatically block that guard from being scheduled.
Do It: Check Your Client's Sites

The Sites list opens as a plain list, grouped by client -- not a card grid. That's deliberate: it's meant to be scannable at a glance.

  • Click into a client's name from the list, or open a client company directly, to see every site under that client, which contract/tender each belongs to, and every shift requirement, all in one place.
  • Open a single site and you'll find three tabs: Posts & Shifts (what's required and when), Contacts & Location (site contact, optional GPS geofence), and Notes & Exclusions (special instructions, and any guard barred from this site).
  • To add a shift requirement to an existing site without running the whole wizard again, open the site and add a row directly under Posts & Shifts.

Now try it. Open the Sites list, pick a client, and find its sites and shift requirements. Come back and mark this done once you can find your way around without help.

Video Walkthrough: Generating and Confirming a Roster

Once client sites and shift requirements are defined, rostering is fast, automated, and deterministic.

What is a Roster Batch?

A roster batch is a scheduling container for a site or client across a date range (e.g., an entire calendar month). It begins in the Draft state.

The 4-Step Rostering Flow:

  1. Open Draft Batch: Open an existing draft batch created by the wizard or click "New" under Rostering to create a batch for your target client/site and date range.
  2. Click "Generate Roster Slots": The system inspects every active shift requirement for the site and builds exact guard slots: 1 slot per guard, per shift, per day across the whole date range.
  3. Auto-Fill or Manual Assignment:
    • Red Highlighted Slots: Indicate unassigned slots awaiting a guard.
    • Auto-Fill Open Slots: The automated allocation algorithm evaluates active security officers, checks shift rest compliance, and enforces guard exclusions to assign eligible guards automatically.
    • Manual Overrides: You can click any slot at any time to select or switch a guard manually.
  4. Click "Confirm Roster": Once satisfied with guard assignments, click Confirm Roster. The status advances to Confirmed.
Immediate Field Deployment: Confirmed means live! Guards can report for duty and be posted against confirmed slots immediately. You do not need to wait for sign-offs before guards start working.
Do It: Generate This Week's Roster

If you set up a client with the onboarding wizard and ticked "Create the first roster batch," a draft batch already exists for that month. Otherwise, open Rostering from the main menu and create a batch for the client/site and date range you need.

  1. Open the roster batch (Draft state).
  2. Click Generate Roster Slots. This reads every active shift requirement for the site and creates one slot per guard, per shift, per day in the range.
  3. Unassigned slots show in red. Use Auto-Fill Open Slots to have the system assign the best eligible guard to each one, or assign guards by hand.
  4. Click Confirm Roster once you're happy. This roster is now live -- guards can be posted against it straight away. There is no separate "make it real" step after this.

You do not need anyone else's sign-off to reach this point. The sign-offs described in the next section happen after the roster is already running, as a check, not a gate.

Now try it. Open a roster batch, generate slots, and confirm it (on a test client/site if you don't want to touch a live one yet). Mark this lesson done once you've seen a batch go from Draft to Confirmed.

Video Walkthrough: Understanding Roster Sign-Offs

The moment a roster batch is generated, a 5-role sign-off sheet is initialized. Here is how sign-offs protect operational integrity without creating bottlenecks.

Sign-Offs Do Not Stop Guards: Guards are already working in the field! Sign-offs exist for accountability, quality control, and cross-departmental auditing -- not as an operational roadblock.

The 5 Sign-Off Roles:

  1. Front Desk: Cross-checks guard assignments against customer post requirements and daily logs.
  2. General Manager: High-level operational validation and site coverage sign-off.
  3. HR: Audits hours equity, guard fatigue rules, and fair shift allocation.
  4. Finance: Validates billable rates and approves payroll readiness.
  5. Director: Retains full executive visibility and oversight.

How Sign-Offs Work:

  • Review: Filter the Roster Sign-Offs menu to view batches awaiting your role's approval.
  • Sign Off: Click "Sign off" if your review passes. You can add an optional comment (e.g. "Checked, guard allocations compliant"). The record stamps your name and date.
  • Flag an Issue: If an irregularity exists (e.g. short-staffed shift, uncertified guard), click "Flag". A written reason is mandatory.
Why Flagging Keeps Operations Running: Flagging a roster records the specific issue for management follow-up while allowing guards to continue protecting the client's premises uninterrupted.
Do It: Check the Sign-Off Sheet

The moment a roster batch is generated, a sign-off row appears for five roles: Front Desk, General Manager, HR, Finance and Director. Each starts Pending.

  • If your role is on the list, open Roster Sign-Offs from the Rostering menu -- it defaults to showing what's waiting on someone.
  • Click Sign off once you've checked your part of the roster. Add a comment if useful; it isn't required to sign.
  • If something's wrong, click Flag instead. A reason is required. Flagging does not stop the roster -- it records that this needs following up, and the roster summary shows who flagged it.
  • You can only sign for a role you actually hold, and you cannot sign a roster you yourself drafted and then also cross-check as Front Desk on the same batch.

Now try it. Open the Roster Sign-Offs list, find a row waiting on a role you hold, and sign it (or flag it with a reason, if you want to see that path). Mark this lesson done once you understand the difference between signing and flagging.

Video Walkthrough: Posting & Reviewing Daily Attendance

Accurate billing and payroll depend on reliable daily attendance recording. DeployGuard ERP uses the Posting Console to manage this workflow.

1. Operations Posts the Shift (Capture)

  1. Operations opens the Posting Console, selects the Site, and chooses the target date.
  2. Every guard scheduled for that shift appears automatically with status Not Marked.
  3. Operations marks each guard as Present, Absent, or AWOL.
  4. Click Save Changes. The batch status becomes Captured.

2. Front Desk Reviews the Shift (Validation)

  1. Front Desk opens the same Posting Console for that site and date.
  2. The batch displays the Captured badge. Front Desk cross-checks the attendance against guard call-ins and incident reports.
  3. Front Desk clicks Review & Validate. The batch moves to Reviewed.
The Segregation-of-Duties Gate: Whoever captures a posting cannot review or validate their own posting. If the same user attempts to perform both actions, the system displays a clear refusal message instructing an independent reviewer to sign off.

If you're Operations: open the Posting Console, pick the site and today's date, and mark each guard Present, Absent or AWOL against their scheduled slot. Save. That's your part done.

If you're Front Desk: your job starts once Operations has posted. Open the same Posting Console for that site and date -- the status badge shows Captured. Check it against what you know actually happened, then click Review & Validate. The batch moves to Reviewed.

One rule holds regardless of role: whoever captured a posting cannot also review it. If you try, the system will tell you plainly why, and name who should review it instead.

Now try it. If you're Operations, post a day's attendance for a real or test site. If you're Front Desk, find a posted batch and review it. Mark this lesson done once you've completed your side of that handoff.
